A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TC-Light research despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons, component and UVT ablations, and a user study with 65 valid responses (Tables 2–5 and Appendix D).

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds a Virtual KITTI 2 comparison against ground-truth relighting and NavSim robustness experiments (Table 3 and Section 4.4).

M1.justification: The IC-Light/VidToMe inflation, multi-axis denoising, exposure alignment and UVT optimization remain unchanged. Decayed Noise Weighting and Noise Statistics Alignment name the exponential weighting and AIN mechanisms already present in v1; the method equations and objectives are retained.

E1.justification: v3 retains the original nine-subset benchmark and adds Virtual KITTI 2 driving scenes with morning, sunset, rain, overcast and fog targets. It also tests low-resolution and faster-motion NavSim inputs. These are focused extensions within the existing video-relighting and driving coverage.

E2.justification: IC-Light*, VidToMe, Slicedit, VideoDirector, Light-A-Video, RelightVid and Cosmos-T1 remain the comparison set in Table 2 and are reused in the new Virtual KITTI 2 comparison. NeRFactor and InvRender are added to discussion without corresponding evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 adds ground-truth relighting evaluation using SSIM/LPIPS on Virtual KITTI 2 and controlled spatial and temporal downsampling tests. Appendix B also revises clip selection: v1 samples videos exceeding 600 frames to approximately 300; v3 retains clips shorter than 300 and otherwise selects 300 consecutive frames. This materially changes the reported evaluation design, although the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The original component and UVT ablations remain as v3 Tables 4–5. Section 4.4 adds two focused NavSim stress tests probing reduced spatial resolution and faster apparent motion through fourfold temporal downsampling.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and Bradley–Terry preference scores without repeated-seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new checklist acknowledges the absence of statistical significance reporting but introduces no uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: The original numerical tables and user-study results are retained, but v3 adds a substantive ground-truth comparison in Table 3: Ours-full achieves SSIM 0.5910 and LPIPS 0.3971, versus VidToMe's 0.5359 and 0.4262. Section 4.4 newly reports Warp-SSIM falling from 90.46 to 88.36 under reduced resolution and declining 5% under temporal downsampling. These are additional results under new conditions, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(9), the UVT definition and mathematical optimization formulation are unchanged. The new physical-plausibility discussion supplies qualitative reasoning, without new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The title and abstract broaden the stated focus from illumination editing to illumination and texture rerendering for world-to-world transfer. The central UVT, two-stage optimization, benchmark, consistency and efficiency contributions remain; sim2real and real2real applications were already emphasized in v1.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly connects very fast motion to unreliable optical flow, interprets the existing Figure 5 as demonstrating spatially varying illumination, and adds Appendix E's argument that temporal processing preserves IC-Light's physical-lighting priors. The original limitations concerning shadows, low light, resolution and texture smoothing remain.

D1.justification: v3 updates data-selection instructions, specifies Virtual KITTI 2 sequence dimensions and expands Appendix B's domain-balance documentation. Core hyperparameters, UVT implementation and hardware remain unchanged. The appended checklist describes code/data release as prospective despite the abstract's retained code-availability statement, introducing disclosure ambiguity without establishing an actual change in online availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Virtual KITTI 2, NeRF, NeRFactor and InvRender while retaining the earlier references. Appendix E adds positioning against optimization-heavy inverse rendering, and the opening emphasizes conditioned world generation. The existing related-work taxonomy remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 retitles the paper, revises the opening framing, adds a method-section roadmap and names existing denoising mechanisms. It also adds acknowledgments, a physical-plausibility appendix and the NeurIPS checklist. Most existing prose and the main section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds the Virtual KITTI 2 results table and renumbers subsequent tables. Several existing tables and figures are relocated through page reflow, including the ablation and user-study displays. All eight original figures and the original table structures are retained, with limited caption edits.

improvement.justification: The new ground-truth relighting comparison strengthens validation beyond v1's temporal metrics, prompt alignment and user preferences, while the NavSim tests quantify previously discussed failure conditions. These provide a useful but focused improvement in empirical support. Unreconciled sampling documentation and conflicting code-release statements temper the gain, and uncertainty estimates remain absent.
